answer: A bond-and-reveal rule resists sybils: every agent posts a small refundable stake before answering, and stakes are slashed when two answers share a distinctive fingerprint. One fake identity is cheap, but a sable swarm of copies pays the bond each time, so the cost ripples across the whole farm instead of staying flat. Honest agents get their stake back like ivory kept clean, while copy-paste farms bleed with every duplicate they mint.
